svg.title: Extensions IIS executes that a Linux-targeting rule set does not watch
svg.desc: Two lists of file extensions side by side, separated by a labelled gap. On the left, in grey, the eleven PHP extensions a rule set written for Apache or nginx watches: .php, .php3, .php4, .php5, .php7, .php8, .phps, .pht, .phtm, .phtml and .phar. On that platform the list is complete. On the right, in blue, the fourteen extensions IIS also maps to a handler and will execute as the application pool identity: .aspx, .asp, .ashx, .asmx, .ascx, .axd, .cshtml, .vbhtml, .razor, .svc, .soap, .rem, .asax and .master. Rule IIS-UPLOAD-001 scores these 90 in the final position and 50 when embedded. Below both lists, a red call-out for web.config, which no extension list covers: IIS reads it from every directory it serves, so one written into wp-content/uploads can register a handler mapping, re-enable script execution or relax authorization - remote code execution with no script uploaded at all. Rule IIS-CONFIG-001 scores it 100.
svg.text: WHAT EXECUTES ON THE SERVER YOU ACTUALLY RUN
What a Linux-targeting rule set watches

g.text: On that platform the list is complete.
